# 1 Clement Chapter 40 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_040_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 40

**40:1** Since therefore these things are plain to us, and we have peered into the depths of the divine knowledge, we ought to perform in orderly fashion all the things that the Master has commanded us to do at their appointed times.

**40:2** He ordained that offerings and ministrations should be carried out, and not at random or in disorder, but at fixed times and hours.

**40:3** Both where and through whom he willed them to be performed, he himself determined by his supreme will: so that all things being done in holiness according to his good pleasure should be well-pleasing to his will.

**40:4** Those, therefore, who present their offerings at the appointed times are accepted and blessed; for following the ordinances of the Master they do not go astray.

**40:5** For to the high priest his own liturgical duties have been assigned; to the priests their own proper place has been appointed; and upon the Levites their own ministries have been laid; the layman is bound by the regulations for laymen.

---

*LOGOS preserves the technical liturgical and ecclesiastical vocabulary: *leitourgiai* (liturgies), *taxis* (order/rank), *kairos* (appointed time/season).*
